items.stem: (i) Define a homologous series of carbon compounds. (ii) Why are the melting and boiling points of C₄H₈ higher than those of C₃H₆ or C₂H₄? (iii) Why do we not see any gradation in the chemical properties of the compounds of a homologous series? (iv) Write the name and structure of (a) an aldehyde and (b) a ketone with the molecular formula C₃H₆O.
items.answer:
(i) A homologous series is a series of compounds with the same general formula and the same functional group, in which any two adjacent members differ by one –CH₂– unit, i.e. by 14 mass units.
(ii) C₂H₄, C₃H₆ and C₄H₈ belong to the same homologous series. As the molecular mass increases along a homologous series a gradation in physical properties is seen: melting and boiling points increase with increasing molecular mass, so C₄H₈ melts and boils at a higher temperature than C₃H₆ or C₂H₄.
(iii) The functional group is the same in every member of a homologous series, and the chemical properties are decided by the functional group, so no gradation in chemical properties is seen.
(iv) (a) Aldehyde: CH₃–CH₂–CHO (propanal)
    (b) Ketone: CH₃–CO–CH₃ (propanone)
items.ocr: LaTeX rewritten to Unicode. The printed definition reads 'differ by CH₂ 14 mass unit'; given here as one –CH₂– unit (14 u). The displayed structures of propanal and propanone were badly broken by OCR (propanal drawn with four carbons), so both are given in condensed form consistent with C₃H₆O.

items.stem: (i) Write the name and structure of an organic compound 'X' having two carbon atoms in its molecule and whose name is suffixed with '-ol'. (ii) What happens when 'X' is heated with excess concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K? Write the chemical equation for the reaction, stating the conditions for the reaction. Also state the role played by concentrated sulphuric acid in the reaction. (iii) Name and draw the electron dot structure of the hydrocarbon produced in the above reaction.
items.answer:
(i) X is ethanol, CH₃–CH₂–OH (H–CH₂–CH₂–O–H drawn out as H–C(H)(H)–C(H)(H)–O–H).
(ii) When ethanol is heated with excess concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K it loses a molecule of water and gives ethene:
CH₃CH₂OH ─(hot conc. H₂SO₄, 443 K)→ CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O
(ethanol → ethene). The concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent, removing water from the ethanol.
(iii) The hydrocarbon produced is ethene. In its electron dot structure each carbon shares two electron pairs with the other carbon (a C=C double bond) and one electron pair with each of two hydrogen atoms, so every carbon completes its octet and every hydrogen its duplet.
items.ocr: Printed 'election dot structure' corrected to 'electron dot structure'. The worked answer for parts (ii) and (iii) sits in an earlier column of the extraction (chars ~140300-140800) and has been rejoined here; the reaction arrow, dropped by MinerU, was restored from it.

items.stem: The formulae of four organic compounds are given below: A: C₂H₄, B: CH₃COOH, C: C₂H₅OH, D: C₂H₆. (i) Which one of these compounds A, B, C or D is a saturated hydrocarbon? (ii) Identify the organic acid and give its structural formula. (iii) Which of the above compounds, when heated at 443 K in the presence of concentrated H₂SO₄, forms ethene as the major product? What is the role played by concentrated H₂SO₄ in this reaction? Also write the chemical equation involved. (iv) Give a chemical equation for the reaction of B and C with each other in the presence of concentrated H₂SO₄. Name the major product formed and mention one of its important uses.
items.answer:
(i) D (C₂H₆, ethane) is the saturated hydrocarbon.
(ii) B (CH₃COOH) is the organic acid. Its structural formula is H–C(H)(H)–C(=O)–O–H, i.e. CH₃–COOH (ethanoic acid).
(iii) C (ethanol, C₂H₅OH) is the compound. Concentrated H₂SO₄ acts as a dehydrating agent and removes a molecule of water from ethanol:
C₂H₅OH ─(hot conc. H₂SO₄, 443 K)→ C₂H₄ (ethene) + H₂O
(iv) CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ─(conc. H₂SO₄)→ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O
(ethanoic acid + ethanol → ethyl ethanoate). The major product is the ester ethyl ethanoate, which is used in making perfumes and as a flavouring agent.

items.stem: (a) A compound X undergoes an addition reaction with H₂ to form a compound Y having molecular mass 30 g mol⁻¹. X decolourises bromine water and burns with a smoky flame. Identify X and Y and write the chemical equations of the reactions involved. (b) Write the structural formulae of (i) butanone and (ii) pentanoic acid. (c) Would you be able to check if water is hard by using a detergent? Give a reason to justify your answer.
items.answer:
(a) X is ethene (C₂H₄) and Y is ethane (C₂H₆), whose molecular mass is 30 g mol⁻¹.
CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ ─(Ni or Pd)→ CH₃–CH₃
X decolourises bromine water and burns with a smoky flame because it is unsaturated.
(b) (i) Butanone: CH₃–CO–CH₂–CH₃
    (ii) Pentanoic acid: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–COOH
(c) No. Detergents are ammonium or sulphonate salts of long chain carboxylic acids, and the ionic ends of these compounds do not form insoluble precipitates with the calcium and magnesium ions present in hard water, so a detergent lathers in hard water just as it does in soft water. Hardness can be checked only with soap, which forms scum on reaction with hard water.

items.stem: Compare soaps and detergents on the basis of their composition and their cleansing action in hard water.
items.answer:
Composition: soaps are the sodium or potassium salts of long chain carboxylic (fatty) acids, whereas detergents are the ammonium or sulphonate salts of long chain carboxylic acids.
Cleansing action in hard water: hard water contains calcium and magnesium salts. These react with soap and form an insoluble white curdy substance called scum, so a large amount of soap is wasted, little lather is formed and the cleansing action is hindered. The charged ends of a detergent do not form an insoluble precipitate with the calcium and magnesium ions of hard water, so detergents lather and clean effectively in hard water as well as in soft water.

items.stem: (a) Write the names and structures of (i) an alcohol and (ii) an aldehyde with four carbon atoms in their molecules. (b) List two differences between saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons.
items.answer:
(a) (i) The alcohol with four carbon atoms is butanol: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–OH.
    (ii) The aldehyde with four carbon atoms is butanal: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CHO.
(b) Hydrocarbons in which all the consecutive carbon atoms are linked by single bonds are called saturated hydrocarbons; those in which the consecutive carbon atoms are linked by at least one double or triple bond are called unsaturated hydrocarbons. Two differences follow from this:
(i) Type of carbon-carbon bond: saturated hydrocarbons have only single covalent bonds, while unsaturated hydrocarbons have at least one double or triple bond.
(ii) Reactivity and stability: saturated hydrocarbons are less reactive and more stable, while unsaturated hydrocarbons are more reactive and less stable. (Their general formulae also differ: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ for alkanes against CₙH₂ₙ for alkenes and CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ for alkynes.)
items.ocr: Printed in the FIVE MARKS block but placed by MinerU inside the THREE MARKS character range (chars 121858-124269); it appears nowhere else in the extraction. The printed structures were broken by OCR - both the alcohol and the aldehyde are drawn with six carbons - so both are given in condensed form with the four carbons the question asks for. The printed answer names only butanol; the aldehyde is named butanal from its drawn structure. items.stem: (a) Draw the electron dot structure of a methane molecule. (b) Identify the functional groups present in the following compounds: (i) C₂H₆O (ii) C₂H₄O. (c) A mixture of oxygen and ethyne is burnt for welding. Why do you think a mixture of ethyne and air is not used for welding?
items.answer:
(a) Methane, CH₄: the carbon atom shares one electron pair with each of four hydrogen atoms, forming four single covalent bonds, so carbon completes its octet and each hydrogen its duplet.
(b) (i) C₂H₆O may be CH₃–CH₂–OH, whose functional group is –OH (alcohol), or CH₃–O–CH₃, whose functional group is –O– (ether).
    (ii) C₂H₄O is CH₃–CHO, whose functional group is –CHO (aldehyde).
(c) Ethyne undergoes incomplete combustion in air and burns with a sooty flame. A mixture of ethyne and oxygen burns with a clean flame at a very high temperature (about 3000 °C) because combustion is complete, and such a high temperature - which welding needs - cannot be attained with air.
items.ocr: MinerU dropped the subscripts in '(i) C H O'; restored to C₂H₆O from the worked answer, which gives ethanol and dimethyl ether. The answer's sentence 'Ethane gives a clean flame with high temperature' is a misprint for the ethyne-oxygen mixture and is corrected.

items.stem: (a) Carry out the following conversions, giving complete conditions for the reaction to take place in each case: (i) Ethanoic acid from ethanol (ii) Ethane from ethene (iii) Ester from ethanoic acid and ethanol. Also state the names given to all the above conversions. (b) Detergents are preferred over soaps. Why? (Give one reason.)
items.answer:
(a) (i) Oxidation: ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid in the presence of an oxidising agent -
C₂H₅OH ─(acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ + heat, or alkaline KMnO₄ + heat)→ CH₃COOH
    (ii) Addition (catalytic hydrogenation): ethene gives ethane in the presence of a nickel catalyst -
CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ ─(Ni catalyst)→ CH₃–CH₃
    (iii) Esterification: CH₃COOH + HO–CH₂CH₃ ─(conc. H₂SO₄ / H⁺)→ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O
The three conversions are called oxidation, hydrogenation (an addition reaction) and esterification respectively.
(b) Detergents are preferred over soaps because they can be used in hard water whereas soaps fail to do so; they also have a stronger cleansing action and form more lather than soap.
items.ocr: The printed solution reads 'On catholic hydro generation ... ethane gives ethane', read as 'on catalytic hydrogenation ... ethene gives ethane'. Missing reaction arrows restored from LaTeX. The figure printed between parts (a) and (b) on page 39 carries the worked structural formulae, not anything the question asks the student to read, so no image is attached.

items.stem: (a) Explain why carbon forms covalent bonds. Give two reasons for carbon forming a large number of compounds. (b) Explain the formation of an ammonia molecule.
items.answer:
(a) Carbon has the electronic configuration 2, 4. It could complete its octet either by gaining four electrons to form a C⁴⁻ anion or by losing four electrons to form a C⁴⁺ cation, but neither is possible on energy considerations - it would need a very large amount of energy to hold ten electrons on a small nucleus, or to remove four electrons. Carbon overcomes this problem by sharing its four valence electrons with other atoms, i.e. by forming covalent bonds. Carbon forms a very large number of compounds because of (i) catenation, its ability to link with other carbon atoms to give long chains, branched chains and rings, and (ii) tetravalency, its ability to bond with four other atoms.
(b) Formation of NH₃: the electronic configuration of nitrogen is 2, 5, so it needs three more electrons to complete its octet; the electronic configuration of hydrogen is 1, so each hydrogen needs one more electron to complete its duplet. One nitrogen atom therefore shares one electron pair with each of three hydrogen atoms, giving three N–H single covalent bonds and one lone pair on nitrogen.

items.stem: (a) Give a chemical test to distinguish between saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons. (b) Name the products formed when ethane burns in air. Write the balanced chemical equation for the reaction, showing the types of energies liberated. (c) Why is the reaction between methane and chlorine in the presence of sunlight considered a substitution reaction?
items.answer:
(a) Bromine water test. Bromine water is a brown coloured liquid. Unsaturated hydrocarbons give an addition reaction with bromine, so the colour of bromine water is decolourised. Saturated hydrocarbons do not react with bromine water, so its colour is not decolourised.
(b) On burning ethane in air the products obtained are carbon dioxide and water, along with heat and light:
2C₂H₆(g) + 7O₂(g) → 4CO₂(g) + 6H₂O(l) + Heat + Light
(c) Methane reacts with chlorine in the presence of sunlight to form chloromethane and hydrogen chloride:
CH₄ + Cl₂ ─(sunlight)→ CH₃Cl + HCl
With excess chlorine all four hydrogen atoms of methane are replaced by chlorine atoms to form carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄). The reaction is considered a substitution reaction because the hydrogen of methane is substituted (replaced) by chlorine.
items.ocr: Printed in the FIVE MARKS block but placed by MinerU inside the THREE MARKS character range (chars 135783-137505); it appears nowhere else in the extraction. Printed 'all the our hydrogen atoms' read as 'all the four hydrogen atoms'. Arrows and subscripts restored from LaTeX.

items.stem: Why are certain compounds called hydrocarbons? Write the general formula for the homologous series of alkanes, alkenes and alkynes and also draw the structure of the first member of each series. Write the name of the reaction that converts alkenes into alkanes and also write a chemical equation to show the necessary conditions for the reaction to occur.
items.answer:
Certain compounds are called hydrocarbons because they are formed mainly from carbon and hydrogen.
General formula for the homologous series of alkanes: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂; of alkenes: CₙH₂ₙ; of alkynes: CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.
First members: methane, CH₄ - one carbon atom joined to four hydrogen atoms by single bonds; ethene, CH₂=CH₂ - two carbon atoms joined by a double bond, each carrying two hydrogen atoms; ethyne, H–C≡C–H - two carbon atoms joined by a triple bond, each carrying one hydrogen atom.
Hydrogenation, an addition reaction, converts alkenes into alkanes:
CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ ─(Pt/Pd/Ni)→ CH₃–CH₃
Dihydrogen gas adds to an alkene in the presence of a finely divided catalyst such as platinum, palladium or nickel to form an alkane.
items.ocr: Printed in the FIVE MARKS block but placed by MinerU inside the THREE MARKS character range (chars 137505-138588); it appears nowhere else in the extraction. Printed 'allkeynes' read as alkynes. The printed solution gives only the three general formulae and the hydrogenation equation - it does not draw the first members the question asks for - so those three structures are described here from their formulae.

items.stem: Soaps and detergents are both types of salts. State the difference between the two. Write the mechanism of the cleaning action of soap. Why do soaps not form lather with hard water? Mention any two problems that arise due to the use of detergents instead of soaps.
items.answer:
Difference: soaps are sodium or potassium salts of long chain carboxylic acids, whereas detergents are ammonium or sulphonate salts of long chain carboxylic acids. Soaps have a lesser cleansing action than detergents, which clean better.
Cleansing action of soap: when soap is dissolved in water it forms a colloidal solution in which the soap molecules cluster together into micelles and remain radially suspended in water, with the hydrocarbon ends towards the centre and the ionic ends directed outward. Dirt particles adhere to the oily or greasy layer present on skin or clothes. When a dirty cloth is dipped into soap solution, the non-polar hydrocarbon ends of the micelles get attached to the grease or oil present in the dirt while the polar ionic ends remain in the water. The mechanical action of rubbing then dislodges the oily layer from the dirty surface, shaping it into small globules, and a stable emulsion of oil in water is formed. The emulsified oil or grease globules, bearing the dirt, can now be readily washed away with water on rinsing.
Soaps do not form lather with hard water because the calcium and magnesium salts present in hard water displace the sodium or potassium ions from the soap molecules, forming an insoluble substance called scum instead of lather.
Two problems that arise from using detergents instead of soaps: (i) detergents are not biodegradable, so they accumulate in the environment and cause pollution; (ii) the entry of detergents into the food chain leads to bioaccumulation in living beings and tends towards health issues.

items.stem: (a) Differentiate between esterification and saponification, giving one example of each. (b) Write any two advantages of detergents over soaps.
items.answer:
(a) Esterification: the process of formation of an ester by the reaction of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid.
CH₃–COOH + H–OCH₂CH₃ ─(conc. H₂SO₄, heat)→ CH₃–COOCH₂CH₃ + H₂O
(ethanoic acid, a carboxylic acid + ethanol, an alcohol → ethyl ethanoate, an ester)
Saponification: esters react in the presence of an acid or a base to give back the alcohol and the carboxylic acid (as its salt when a base is used). This reaction is known as saponification.
CH₃COOC₂H₅ + NaOH → C₂H₅OH + CH₃COONa
(b) Advantages of detergents over soaps: (i) they can be used even in hard water; (ii) they can be used even in acidic medium; (iii) they produce lather much more easily than soaps; (iv) their cleansing power is much higher than that of soaps; (v) they are more soluble in water than soaps.
items.ocr: The printed saponification equation shows NaOH over the arrow but writes the acid product as CH₃COOH; with NaOH the product is the sodium salt CH₃COONa, so the equation is given balanced that way. Arrows restored from LaTeX. A tail fragment of another question's answer about scum, which MinerU placed just above this question, was stripped.

items.stem: What are covalent compounds? Why are they different from ionic compounds? List their three characteristic properties.
items.answer:
Covalent compounds are the compounds containing covalent bonds, i.e. bonds formed by the sharing of electron pairs between atoms. They differ from ionic compounds because ionic compounds are made of oppositely charged ions held by strong electrostatic forces, while covalent compounds are made of neutral molecules held by weak intermolecular forces.
IonicCompoundsCovalent Compounds
They have high melting points and high point. boilingC 0 v a e n t compounds have usually low points and points. melting boiling
They conduct electricity when dissolved in water or melted.They do not conduct electricity.
They are usually soluble in water.They are usually insoluble in water (except, glucose sugar, urea, etc.)
Characteristic properties of covalent compounds: (i) They have low melting and boiling points. (ii) They do not conduct electricity. (iii) They are usually insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents.

items.stem: An organic compound with molecular formula C₂H₄O₂ produces brisk effervescence on addition of sodium carbonate or sodium hydrogencarbonate. (a) Identify the organic compound. (b) Name the gas evolved. (c) How will you test the gas evolved? (d) Write a chemical equation for the above reaction. (e) List two important uses of the above compound.
items.answer:
(a) The organic compound is ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH.
(b) The gas evolved is carbon dioxide.
(c) Pass the gas evolved through lime water. If the lime water turns milky, the gas evolved is carbon dioxide.
(d) CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → CH₃COONa + CO₂ + H₂O
    Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O (the test with lime water)
(e) (i) A dilute solution of ethanoic acid is used to preserve pickles. (ii) On reaction with alcohols it produces esters, which are used in making perfumes and as flavouring agents.
items.ocr: The printed question number was lost in the extraction; inferred as 260 from its position between printed 259 and 261 (260 appears nowhere else in the chapter). The formula printed as 'C H O 2' was restored to C₂H₄O₂ from the worked answer. Arrows restored from LaTeX.

items.stem: (a) Why does carbon form the largest number of compounds? Give two reasons. (b) Why are some of these called saturated and the others unsaturated compounds? (c) Which of these two is more reactive and why? (d) Draw the structures of the following compounds: (i) Bromopentane (ii) Hexanal.
items.answer:
(a) Carbon forms a large number of compounds because of (i) Catenation - carbon forms bonds with other atoms of carbon, giving long chains, branched chains and rings; and (ii) Tetravalency - carbon shares its four valence electrons with four other atoms.
(b) Some compounds are called saturated because they contain only single bonds between two carbon atoms, while others are termed unsaturated because in them the valency of carbon is satisfied by a double or a triple bond.
(c) Unsaturated compounds are more reactive, because the double or triple bond makes them less stable than saturated compounds. They react readily to satisfy their valency with single bonds and so become stable.
(d) (i) Bromopentane: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–Br (C₅H₁₁Br)
    (ii) Hexanal: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–CHO (C₆H₁₂O)
items.ocr: The printed number '261.' is set inside the stem line ('Why does carbon form largest number of 261. compounds ?') and has been moved back to the head of the question. The displayed structures in (d) show extra carbon atoms after OCR (six carbons for bromopentane, ten for hexanal), so both are given in condensed form matching their correct formulae.

items.stem: (a) Write chemical equations for the reactions of ethanoic acid with (i) sodium, (ii) sodium carbonate, (iii) ethanol in the presence of conc. H₂SO₄. (b) State the role of concentrated sulphuric acid in the esterification reaction. (c) Write one use of ethanoic acid.
items.answer:
(a) (i) 2CH₃COOH + 2Na → 2CH₃COONa + H₂
    (ii) 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + CO₂ + H₂O
    (iii) CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ─(conc. H₂SO₄)→ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O
(b) Sulphuric acid, being a strong dehydrating agent, removes water from the reaction mixture. As a result the reaction proceeds only in the forward direction to form the ester.
(c) Ethanoic acid is used for making vinegar.
items.ocr: Printed equation (a)(ii) ends '+ CO₂ + H₂'; corrected to '+ CO₂ + H₂O' as required for balance and as the same reaction is printed elsewhere in this chapter. Missing arrows restored from LaTeX.

items.stem: An organic compound A is widely used as a preservative in pickles and has a molecular formula C₂H₄O₂. This compound reacts with ethanol to form a sweet smelling compound B. (a) Identify the compound A. (b) Write the chemical equation for the reaction with ethanol to form compound B. (c) How can we get compound A from B? (d) Name the process and write the corresponding chemical equation. (e) Which gas is produced when compound A reacts with washing soda? Write the chemical equation.
items.answer:
(a) A is ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH.
(b) CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ─(conc. H₂SO₄)→ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O (B is ethyl ethanoate).
(c) Compound A can be obtained back from compound B by the action of an acid or a base on the ester.
(d) The process is saponification:
CH₃COOC₂H₅ + NaOH → C₂H₅OH + CH₃COONa
(e) CO₂ gas is produced:
2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂
items.ocr: Missing reaction arrows restored from LaTeX. The printed saponification line writes CH₃COOH as the product over NaOH; with NaOH the product is the sodium salt, so it is written as CH₃COONa.

items.stem: Answer the following questions: (a) Describe a chemical test to distinguish between ethanol and ethanoic acid. (b) Give reasons for the following: (i) Ethanol is used in the preparation of tincture iodine. (ii) Ethanoic acid is used in the preservation of pickles.
items.answer:
(a) Ethanol and ethanoic acid can be distinguished using sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) solution as the laboratory reagent.
(i) When Na₂CO₃ is added to the test tube containing ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH), CO₂ gas is evolved with brisk effervescence, and the gas turns lime water milky.
(ii) When Na₂CO₃ is added to the test tube containing ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH), no gas is evolved.
(b) (i) Ethanol is used in the preparation of tincture iodine because it acts as a solvent for iodine.
    (ii) Ethanoic acid is used in the preservation of pickles because it kills bacteria.
items.ocr: Page furniture 'Click Here to Buy book on Amazon' and the page break between the stem and part (b) of the answer were stripped.

items.stem: (a) An organic compound A is widely used as a preservative in pickles and has a molecular formula C₂H₄O₂. This compound reacts with ethanol in the presence of a mineral acid to form a sweet smelling compound B. (i) Identify the compound A. (ii) Which gas is produced when A reacts with sodium carbonate? Write the balanced chemical equation for the reaction involved. (b) Write the names of: (i) CH₃CH₂Br (ii) CH₃–CH=CH₂.
items.answer:
(a) (i) A is ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH).
    (ii) Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is produced:
2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂
(b) (i) CH₃CH₂Br is bromoethane.
    (ii) CH₃–CH=CH₂ is propene.

items.stem: (a) Answer the following questions in one sentence or one word: (i) What type of organic compounds show substitution reactions? (ii) How will you convert ethanol into an unsaturated hydrocarbon? (iii) How is a carboxylic acid different from mineral acids? (b) With the help of electron dot representation, explain the formation of an O₂ molecule.
items.answer:
(a) (i) Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) show substitution reactions.
    (ii) By dehydration of the alcohol with excess concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K:
C₂H₅OH ─(hot conc. H₂SO₄, 443 K)→ CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O
    (iii) Mineral acids are strong acids because they ionise completely in water, whereas carboxylic acids are weak acids because they do not ionise completely.
(b) Atomic number of oxygen = 8; electronic configuration = 2, 6. Each oxygen atom has six valence electrons and needs two more to complete its octet, so the two atoms share two electron pairs between them. This gives a double bond between the two oxygen atoms, O=O.
items.ocr: The printed answer to (a)(i) is cut off after 'Saturated hydrocarbons or'; completed as alkanes. The figure on page 43 next to this question is the electron dot diagram of O₂ belonging to the worked answer, so no image is attached.

items.stem: An organic compound A on heating with conc. H₂SO₄ forms a compound B, which on addition of one mole of hydrogen in the presence of nickel forms a compound C. One mole of C on combustion forms two moles of CO₂ and three moles of H₂O. Identify the compounds A, B and C and write the equations for the reactions involved.
items.answer:
Compound A is ethanol, compound B is ethene and compound C is ethane.
C₂H₅OH ─(conc. H₂SO₄, Δ)→ CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O
CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ ─(Ni)→ CH₃–CH₃
2C₂H₆ + 7O₂ → 4CO₂ + 6H₂O (so one mole of ethane gives two moles of CO₂ and three moles of H₂O)
items.ocr: The printed stem reads 'two/three moles of H₂O', an OCR merge of the option; the worked solution identifies C as ethane, whose combustion gives three moles of H₂O per mole, so 'three' is used and the conflict is recorded here. Missing arrows restored from LaTeX.

items.stem: Identify the compounds A to E in the following reaction sequence: (a) CH₃CH₂OH ─(KMnO₄/KOH, then dil. HCl)→ A (b) CH₃CH₂OH + A ─(conc. H₂SO₄)→ B + H₂O (c) B + NaOH → C + CH₃CH₂OH (d) A + NaHCO₃ → C + D + H₂O (e) CH₃CH₂OH + E → CH₃CH₂ONa + H₂
items.answer:
(a) CH₃CH₂OH ─(KMnO₄/KOH, then dil. HCl)→ CH₃COOH + H₂O, so A = ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH).
(b) CH₃CH₂OH + CH₃COOH ─(conc. H₂SO₄)→ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O, so B = ethyl ethanoate (an ester).
(c) CH₃COOC₂H₅ + NaOH → CH₃COONa + CH₃CH₂OH, so C = sodium ethanoate (CH₃COONa).
(d) CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → CH₃COONa + CO₂ + H₂O, so D = carbon dioxide (CO₂).
(e) 2CH₃CH₂OH + 2Na → 2CH₃CH₂ONa + H₂, so E = sodium (Na).
items.ocr: The printed reaction scheme was heavily mangled by OCR (labels a-e detached from their equations and the ester drawn as CH₃CH₂-CO-O-CH₃); the five steps were rebuilt from the printed worked solution and the missing arrows restored.

items.stem: Write chemical equations to represent what happens when: (a) Ethanol burns in air. (b) Ethanol reacts with sodium metal. (c) Ethanol is heated with alkaline KMnO₄. (d) Ethanol is heated with ethanoic acid in the presence of a few drops of concentrated sulphuric acid. (e) Ethanol is heated at 443 K with excess concentrated H₂SO₄.
items.answer:
(a) CH₃CH₂OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O + heat and light
(b) 2CH₃CH₂OH + 2Na → 2CH₃CH₂ONa + H₂
(c) CH₃CH₂OH ─(alkaline KMnO₄)→ CH₃COOH
(d) CH₃CH₂OH + CH₃COOH ─(conc. H₂SO₄)→ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O
(e) CH₃CH₂OH ─(excess conc. H₂SO₄, 443 K)→ CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O
items.ocr: Printed equation (a) is unbalanced ('CH₃CH₂OH + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + Heat'); balanced here. The printed product of (e) is typeset as 'C₂H₂', which contradicts its own condition line and the rest of the chapter - dehydration of ethanol gives ethene, CH₂=CH₂ (C₂H₄), so the solution wins. Arrows restored.

(ii) CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂↑

items.stem: (a) The formula of an ester is CH₃COOC₂H₅. Write the structural formulae of the corresponding alcohol and the acid. (b) (i) Mention the experimental conditions involved in obtaining ethene from ethanol. (ii) Write the chemical equation for the above reaction.
items.answer:
(a) Alcohol: ethanol, H–C(H)(H)–C(H)(H)–OH, i.e. CH₃–CH₂–OH.
    Acid: ethanoic acid, H–C(H)(H)–C(=O)–OH, i.e. CH₃–COOH.
(b) (i) The ethanol is heated up to 443 K in the presence of excess concentrated H₂SO₄, which acts as a dehydrating agent.
    (ii) CH₃–CH₂OH ─(hot conc. H₂SO₄, 443 K)→ CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O
items.ocr: The displayed structural formulae in the printed answer were broken by OCR (ethanol drawn with a stray extra H); rewritten in condensed Unicode form. Reaction arrow restored.

items.stem: (a) What is vinegar? Give its use. (b) Name two properties of carbon which led to the huge number of carbon compounds we see around us. (c) Give a chemical test to distinguish between butter and cooking oil. (d) Why does carbon form compounds having low melting and boiling points?
items.answer:
(a) A 5 to 8% solution of acetic acid (ethanoic acid) in water is called vinegar. It is used as a preservative in pickles.
(b) Catenation and tetravalency.
(c) Alkaline potassium permanganate can be used to distinguish between butter and cooking oil. Cooking oil decolourises the pink colour of alkaline potassium permanganate whereas butter does not. This shows that cooking oil is unsaturated and butter is saturated.
(d) The forces of attraction between the molecules of carbon compounds are not very strong, because carbon compounds are covalent. Thus carbon forms compounds having low melting and boiling points.
items.ocr: The printed part label '(c)' was OCR'd as a bare capital 'C' run into the sentence; restored.

items.stem: (a) Draw the structure of ethanoic acid. (b) Name the compound formed when ethanol is heated with ethanoic acid in the presence of conc. H₂SO₄. (c) Complete the following equations: (i) CH₄ + Cl₂ ─(sunlight)→ (ii) C₂H₅OH + O₂ ─(combustion)→
items.answer:
(a) Ethanoic acid: H–C(H)(H)–C(=O)–OH, i.e. CH₃–COOH.
(b) Ethyl ethanoate (ethyl acetate).
(c) (i) CH₄ + Cl₂ ─(sunlight)→ CH₃Cl + HCl
    (ii) C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ ─(combustion)→ 2CO₂ + 3H₂O
items.ocr: The printed skeleton equations in (c) lost their arrows ('CH4 + Cl2 Sunlight', 'C H OH + O2 Combustion'); arrows and subscripts restored from the worked answer on the next page.

items.stem: (a) Complete the following reactions and name the main product formed in each case: (i) CH₃COOH + NaOH → ..... + ..... (ii) C₂H₅OH + O₂ → ..... + ..... (iii) (CH₃)₂C=C(CH₃)₂ + H₂ ─(Ni catalyst)→ (b) What is a covalent bond? How many such bonds are present in ethane? Write two characteristic features of covalent compounds.
items.answer:
(a) (i) CH₃COOH + NaOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O; the main product is sodium ethanoate.
    (ii) C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O + heat and light; this is the combustion of ethanol and the main products are carbon dioxide and water.
    (iii) (CH₃)₂C=C(CH₃)₂ + H₂ ─(Ni catalyst)→ (CH₃)₂CH–CH(CH₃)₂; the main product is the saturated hydrocarbon 2,3-dimethylbutane.
(b) A covalent bond is a bond formed by the sharing of an electron pair between two atoms. Ethane (C₂H₆) contains seven single covalent bonds - six C–H bonds and one C–C bond. Characteristic features of covalent compounds: (i) they have low melting and boiling points; (ii) they are generally gaseous or liquid substances; (iii) they are bad conductors of electricity and heat; (iv) they are of two types, polar and non-polar.
items.ocr: The printed structure in (a)(iii) is a tetramethyl-substituted alkene, but the printed answer names the hydrogenation product 'Hexene' - which is neither saturated nor consistent with the drawn structure. The drawn structure and the worked hydrogenation win, so the product is given as 2,3-dimethylbutane and the conflict is recorded. The printed part labels show '(ii)' twice; relabelled (ii) and (iii). Printed (a)(ii) is unbalanced; balanced here.

items.stem: (a) Write a chemical equation for the combustion of ethanol. (b) List any two differences between saturated and unsaturated carbon compounds.
items.answer:
(a) CH₃CH₂OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O + heat and light
(b) (i) Compounds of carbon that have only single bonds between the carbon atoms are called saturated compounds, whereas compounds of carbon which contain double or triple bonds between the carbon atoms are called unsaturated compounds.
    (ii) Saturated compounds usually burn with a clean blue flame and are less reactive, whereas unsaturated compounds burn with a sooty flame and are more reactive than saturated ones.

items.stem: (a) Complete the following reactions, stating the main products formed in each: (i) CH₃–CH=CH₂ + H₂ ─(Ni catalyst)→ (ii) C₂H₅OH + Na → (iii) CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → (b) Write the next homologue of propanol (CH₃CH₂CH₂OH) and of butanal (CH₃CH₂CH₂CHO).
items.answer:
(a) (i) CH₃–CH=CH₂ + H₂ ─(Ni catalyst)→ CH₃CH₂CH₃ (propane)
    (ii) 2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂ (sodium ethoxide)
    (iii) 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂ (sodium ethanoate)
(b) The next homologue of propanol is butanol, CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH. The next homologue of butanal is pentanal, CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CHO.

items.stem: (a) Define catenation. Why does no other element exhibit catenation to the extent seen in carbon compounds? (b) Name the type of compound formed by the reaction of an organic acid and an alcohol. Write the chemical equation for the reaction involved.
items.answer:
(a) Catenation is the self-linking property of an element due to which a large number of its atoms can be linked with each other by covalent bonds to form a chain. No other element except carbon possesses this self-linking property to an extent that lets it form large compounds as long chains, so no other element exhibits catenation to the extent seen in carbon compounds.
(b) An ester is formed by the reaction of an organic (carboxylic) acid and an alcohol; the reaction is called esterification.
CH₃COOH + CH₃CH₂OH ─(conc. H₂SO₄)→ CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ + H₂O
(ethanoic acid + ethanol → ethyl ethanoate)
items.ocr: The printed stem is scrambled by the two-column OCR ('Define catenation. Why no other element the properties of 277. exhibits catenation to the extent seen in carbon compounds ?'); the stray words 'the properties of' and the misplaced number were removed. The printed answer breaks off mid-sentence after 'a large number of its atoms can be linked' at a page break; its continuation, including the whole of (b), prints further on in the extraction at the head of the page that carries question 278, and has been rejoined here. The esterification equation printed there carries no arrow or conditions; both are restored from the same reaction printed elsewhere in this chapter.

items.stem: (a) Write balanced equations for the following reactions: (i) CH₃OH + Na → (ii) CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → (iii) C₂H₆ + O₂ (excess) → (b) Write the formula and name of the next homologue of: (i) CH₃CH=CH₂ and (ii) CH₃–CO–CH₃.
items.answer:
(a) (i) 2CH₃OH + 2Na → 2CH₃ONa + H₂ (sodium methoxide)
    (ii) CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂ (sodium acetate, i.e. sodium ethanoate)
    (iii) 2C₂H₆ + 7O₂ → 4CO₂ + 6H₂O + Heat + Light
(b) (i) The next homologue of propene (CH₃CH=CH₂) is butene, CH₃CH₂CH=CH₂ (C₄H₈).
    (ii) The next homologue of propanone (CH₃–CO–CH₃) is butanone, CH₃CH₂–CO–CH₃ (C₄H₈O).

items.stem: (a) What is a catalyst? Write the chemical equation to represent the hydrogenation of ethene. (b) Which of the following compounds belong to the same homologous series? C₂H₆, C₂H₄O₂, C₂H₆O, C₄H₁₀
items.answer:
(a) A catalyst is a substance that causes a reaction to occur, or to proceed at a different rate, without the catalyst itself being affected by the reaction.
Hydrogenation of ethene: CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ ─(nickel catalyst)→ CH₃–CH₃
(b) C₂H₆ and C₄H₁₀ belong to the same homologous series - both are alkanes, CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, differing by two –CH₂– units.

(iii) Reaction of ethanol with sodium metal. (b) What are isomers? Write any two possible structures for the formula C₅H₁₂.
items.answer:
(a) (i) CH₃CH₂OH ─(hot conc. H₂SO₄, 443 K)→ CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O
    (ii) CH₃CH₂OH + CH₃COOH ─(conc. H₂SO₄ / H⁺)→ CH₃–CO–OC₂H₅ + H₂O

(i) Pentane: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃
(ii) 2-methylbutane: CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃

items.stem: Complete the following reactions and name the main product formed in each case: (i) CH₃CH₂OH + 2[O] ─(acidified K₂Cr₂O₇)→ (ii) CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → (iii) CH₃COOC₂H₅ + NaOH →

(ii) CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂; the main product is sodium ethanoate (sodium acetate).

items.stem: (a) Complete the following reactions and state the main product formed in each case: (i) CH₄ + Cl₂ ─(sunlight)→ (ii) CH₃CH₂OH ─(conc. H₂SO₄)→ (b) State in brief a chemical test to distinguish between ethanol and ethanoic acid.
items.answer:
(a) (i) CH₄ + Cl₂ ─(sunlight)→ CH₃Cl + HCl; the main product is chloromethane.
    (ii) CH₃CH₂OH ─(conc. H₂SO₄)→ CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O; the main product is ethene.
(b) Add sodium hydrogencarbonate (NaHCO₃) to each liquid. Ethanoic acid reacts with NaHCO₃ and gives brisk effervescence of CO₂ gas, but ethanol does not react with NaHCO₃ and no gas is evolved.

items.stem: (a) Amongst soaps and detergents, which can work effectively in hard water and why? (b) Name the salts which cause hardness of water. (c) What change will you observe if you test soap with litmus paper (red and blue)?
items.answer:
(a) Detergents work more effectively in hard water. They are ammonium or sulphonate salts of long chain hydrocarbons, and the charged ends of these compounds do not form an insoluble precipitate with the calcium and magnesium ions present in hard water, whereas soaps form an insoluble precipitate with hard water which hinders their cleansing action. Detergents therefore clean more effectively.
(b) The salts that lead to hardness of water are the chlorides and sulphates of calcium and magnesium, i.e. CaCl₂, MgCl₂, CaSO₄ and MgSO₄.
(c) Soap solution turns red litmus paper blue, while there is no effect on blue litmus paper. This indicates that soaps are basic in nature.

items.stem: (I) Complete the following reactions: (a) C₂H₅OH + CH₃COOH ─(conc. H₂SO₄)→ (b) CH₄ + Cl₂ ─(sunlight)→ ..... + HCl (c) CH₃CH₂OH ─(hot conc. H₂SO₄)→ ..... + H₂O (II) State two properties of carbon which lead to the huge number of carbon compounds we see around us.
items.answer:
(I) (a) C₂H₅OH + CH₃COOH ─(conc. H₂SO₄)→ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O
    (b) CH₄ + Cl₂ ─(sunlight)→ CH₃Cl + HCl
    (c) CH₃CH₂OH ─(hot conc. H₂SO₄)→ H₂C=CH₂ + H₂O
(II) (i) Catenation: carbon has the unique ability to form bonds with other atoms of carbon, giving rise to a large number of molecules. This property is called catenation.
    (ii) Tetravalency: since carbon has a valency of four, it is capable of bonding with four other atoms of carbon or atoms of other monovalent elements. In order to satisfy its tetravalency, carbon can also form double or triple bonds with other carbon atoms or with oxygen and nitrogen.

items.stem: (a) An organic compound A is a liquid at room temperature. It is also a good solvent and has the molecular formula C₂H₆O. On oxidation it gives compound B, which gives effervescence with sodium hydrogencarbonate. A reacts with B in the presence of conc. sulphuric acid to give another compound C, which has a pleasant smell. Identify A and C. Also write the chemical equations for the reactions involved in the formation of B and C. (b) Draw the structures of benzene (C₆H₆) and cyclohexane (C₆H₁₂). (c) What is the difference between vegetable oil and animal fat?
items.answer:
(a) A is ethyl alcohol (ethanol, C₂H₅OH) and C is an ester, ethyl ethanoate (CH₃COOC₂H₅); B is ethanoic acid (acetic acid).
(i) Formation of B: C₂H₅OH ─(oxidation with alkaline KMnO₄ or acidified K₂Cr₂O₇)→ CH₃COOH
(ii) Formation of C: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ─(conc. H₂SO₄)→ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O
(b) Benzene, C₆H₆, is a ring of six carbon atoms with alternate single and double bonds, each carbon carrying one hydrogen atom. Cyclohexane, C₆H₁₂, is a ring of six carbon atoms joined by single bonds only, each carbon carrying two hydrogen atoms.
(c) Vegetable oil contains unsaturated fatty acids while animal fat contains saturated fatty acids.

items.stem: (a) Write the molecular formula of an organic compound having its name suffixed with '-ol' and having two carbon atoms in the molecule. With the help of a balanced chemical equation indicate what happens when it is heated with excess of concentrated H₂SO₄. (b) Write the names of the following compounds: (i) HCOOH (ii) CH₃COCH₂CH₃. (c) Explain why carbon generally forms compounds by covalent bonds.
items.answer:
(a) The compound is ethanol; its molecular formula is C₂H₅OH (C₂H₆O). When it is heated with excess of concentrated H₂SO₄ it is dehydrated and ethene is formed:
CH₃CH₂OH ─(conc. H₂SO₄, 443 K)→ CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O
(b) (i) HCOOH is methanoic acid. (ii) CH₃COCH₂CH₃ is butanone.
(c) Carbon generally forms covalent compounds because it can neither donate nor accept four electrons to complete its octet - both would require a very large amount of energy. It therefore shares its four valence electrons with other atoms, forming covalent bonds.

items.stem: (a) Draw and write the names of any two structural isomers of C₅H₁₂. (b) Discuss the drawback of using soaps over detergents for the cleansing process.
items.answer:
(a) Two structural isomers of C₅H₁₂:
(i) Pentane: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃
(ii) 2-methylbutane: CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃
(b) Soaps form an insoluble substance called scum with hard water, because they react with the calcium and magnesium salts which cause the hardness of water. A much larger amount of soap then has to be used for cleansing. This is the main drawback of using soap rather than a detergent for the cleansing process.

items.stem: (a) Draw the structure of propanoic acid (C₂H₅COOH). (b) Why do the bottoms of cooking vessels get blackened? (c) What is a micelle? Draw a labelled diagram of a micelle.
items.answer:
(a) Propanoic acid: CH₃–CH₂–COOH, i.e. H–C(H)(H)–C(H)(H)–C(=O)–O–H.
(b) The air holes of the burner sometimes get blocked, and the fuel then burns incompletely. Incomplete burning releases a great deal of soot, which blackens the bottoms of the cooking vessels.
(c) A micelle is the structure formed when soap molecules arrange and align themselves in water with their ionic ends in the water and their hydrocarbon 'tails' held out of it. In a labelled diagram the micelle is drawn as a spherical cluster of soap molecules, each molecule shown as a small circle (the ionic, water-loving head) with a zig-zag tail (the hydrocarbon, water-repelling end); the heads point outwards into the water and the tails point inwards, surrounding the drop of oil or grease.

items.stem: (a) Draw the structure of: (i) Chloropentane (C₅H₁₁Cl) (ii) Ethanoic acid. (b) How is scum formed? (c) Write the names of the following compounds: (i) CH₃–CO–CH₃ (ii) CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CHO
items.answer:
(a) (i) Chloropentane: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–Cl
    (ii) Ethanoic acid: CH₃–C(=O)–O–H, i.e. CH₃COOH
(b) When soap reacts with hard water, the minerals (the calcium and magnesium salts) present in the water react with the soap and form a white curdy substance known as scum. It reduces the cleansing ability of the soap.
(c) (i) Propanone (ii) Butanal

items.stem: (a) A compound X having the formula C₂H₄O₂, when treated with ethanol and a few drops of conc. H₂SO₄, forms a sweet smelling substance Y. Name X and Y. Write the equation of the reaction leading to the formation of Y from X. What is the function of conc. H₂SO₄ in the above reaction? (b) Why do soaps form scum instead of lather in hard water?
items.answer:
(a) X is ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH) and Y is ethyl ethanoate (CH₃COOC₂H₅).
CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ─(conc. H₂SO₄)→ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O
Conc. H₂SO₄ acts as a catalyst and as a dehydrating agent: it removes water from the product mixture, so the reaction proceeds in the forward direction.
(b) Hard water contains calcium and magnesium ions, which react with soap to form insoluble calcium and magnesium salts. These insoluble salts hinder lather formation and separate out, so soaps form scum instead of lather in hard water.

items.stem: Compound A (C₂H₆O) is obtained by reacting a compound B with water in the presence of phosphoric acid. A burns in air with a blue flame to form CO₂ and H₂O. On reacting with K₂Cr₂O₇ it produces compound C, which turns blue litmus red. Identify the compounds A, B and C. Write the chemical equations involved in all the reactions.
items.answer:
A is obtained by the addition of water to another compound B, so A is an alcohol and B is an alkene. With the given molecular formula C₂H₆O, A is ethanol and B is ethene; C, which turns blue litmus red, is ethanoic acid.
CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O ─(H₃PO₄)→ CH₃–CH₂–OH (ethanol, A)
CH₃–CH₂–OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O (A burns in air with a blue flame)
CH₃–CH₂–OH ─(K₂Cr₂O₇)→ CH₃COOH (ethanoic acid, C)
